Good morning from Brookfield Academy Ground at Riverside, where Northmere won the toss, chose to field, and then controlled almost every meaningful piece of the cricket that was actually completed before the match was abandoned, even though the scorecard also shows enough extras to remind you that this was not a perfectly clean bowling session. The opening overs gave Northmere exactly the kind of grip a fielding side wants after choosing to bowl first.

Good afternoon from Southbank Oval in Fairhaven, where Fairmont chose to bat and ended up producing the kind of innings that feels ordinary only if you glance at the final total too quickly, because their 318 all out was not built in one smooth climb but in a set of sharply different phases: a controlled start, a quick captain’s lift, a long middle repair, and then a late burst so violent that Westmere were left chasing not just a large score but the emotional damage of having watched the innings get away after they had created several chances to pull it back. Luca Ford and Aiden Carter gave Fairmont a steady enough beginning, not a spectacular one, but a useful one, because the first job after choosing to bat was to prevent Westmere from turning the new ball into a sequence of early breakthroughs.
